summary_responses.response: In microservice architectures, temporary capacity miscoordination can cause overloads that reject high-value transactions and trigger performance-degrading retry storms when standard retry mechanisms are used. To address this vulnerability, researchers propose DiffTry (Differential Retries), a lightweight, stateless mechanism that assigns class-specific retry limits to prioritize critical requests. By granting high-priority transactions more retry attempts than low-priority ones, DiffTry transforms standard retries into a distributed rejection-prioritization tool without requiring explicit overload detection or inter-service coordination. The authors developed a comprehensive analytical framework to model DiffTry's behavior across single services and complex networks, providing formal mathematical guarantees regarding its convergence and effectiveness. Extensive simulations and a live Kubernetes deployment validated the theoretical model, demonstrating that DiffTry successfully protects high-priority traffic and mitigates the impact of both incidental and adversarial overloads.

summary_responses.response: The Federal Aviation Administration has issued a final rule adopting a new airworthiness directive for certain Bombardier Model BD-700-2A12 airplanes to address unsafe low clearance conditions in the right wing. These low clearance issues occur between fuel line flexible couplings, harness support brackets, hydraulic systems, and fuel vent tubes, which could potentially create an ignition source in the fuel tank during a lightning strike. Prompted by a similar mandate from Transport Canada, this final rule will officially go into effect on November 18, 2026.

summary_responses.subtopic: Public Administration, Labor Policy & Family Leave
summary_responses.response: The Office of Personnel Management is issuing a direct final rule to update its Family and Medical Leave Act and Paid Parental Leave regulations to reflect recent statutory amendments. Under the new rule, virtually all types of Federal civilian service, including temporary and intermittent employment, will now count toward the twelve-month service requirement for leave eligibility. Additionally, the revisions allow certain honorable active military service in the armed forces to be credited toward this same twelve-month eligibility requirement. The updated regulations also clarify that annual and sick leave earned under non-title 5 authorities can be substituted for unpaid leave, while explicitly excluding certain Veterans Health Administration employees from title 5 coverage. This direct final rule will become effective on December 14, 2026, provided the agency does not receive significant adverse comments during the public comment period.
